title: Jev for the tick's starting tier only: skip role ticks, route on probability mass, measure the threshold
description:
Operator, 2026-09-28: 'last thing i wanna do is to use jev to use jev. only clear value cases.' The one clear case is the starting tier: without it every tick starts on pi/GLM and big ones burn an hour before escalating (46x, dz1 in epic-6in), and the 2026-09-22 evaluation (49 ticks, $0.0022) showed labels above ~0.75 confidence match human judgement. Do: skip ticks that carry a role; route to the expensive tier when P(design)+P(diagnosis) > threshold; measure the threshold on history (the 49-tick wne set plus 2jn/6in ticks with their actual outcomes); record each classification on the run branch so a resume replays it.

Considered and NOT doing unless a real failure shows a rule can't cover it: report-honesty checks (the gate and CI verify the work, not the report's claim), finding gating prediction (the reporter's-claim rule plus the absorption fixes hold), live-demo detection (#92's rule), BLOCKED question classes (the frontier worker applies the standing orders itself), stuck disambiguation (activity signals plus a nudge), prose-acceptance mapping (#100 backlogs).
notes:
2026-09-30 13:16 - THRESHOLD MEASUREMENT (2026-09-30): mass_threshold = 0.75

DATASET. 108 role-less implement ticks. The 49-set (9pd 27 / dha 14 / ncv 8,
rebuilt; role ticks h0f, pxc, 3q0 dropped -> 46), plus 2jn 45, 6in 8 and hn6 9.
The 09-22 per-tick distributions were never saved, so every tick was re-asked
with the production client (jev.Client.Classify, one tick per call, the same
credential path as run-epic), twice. Recorded classifications were used where
they exist: bib (6in) and r5i/3gk/7uv/ltg (hn6 cloud). The re-asks agree with
them. Drift between the two asks: mean |d mass| 0.011, max 0.09; argmax agreed
on 104/108.

OUTCOMES come from the run event logs (and `ticfac events` for hn6) plus the
attempt branches. 96 ticks have a known outcome; hn6's are unknown because its
cloud runs failed on infrastructure only. There are two labels:
  - FAILED (the metric ms9 asks about: a cheap start that failed and then
    escalated): a wall-clock or stuck kill, a work rejection, or a tier
    escalation. 10 ticks.
  - HARD (broad): FAILED, or any attempt with more than 60 min of work time.
    32 ticks.
Process failures do not count: merge conflicts, holds, stale evidence, the
absorption bound, start failures.

SWEEP (strict >, N=96):
  T     dear  misses(FAILED)  misses(HARD)
  0.20   47        7              21
  0.40   38        7              22
  0.50   34        7              24
  0.60   29        7              25
  0.75   22        7              25
  0.80   19        7              26
Argmax in {design, diagnosis}: 38 dear, 22 HARD misses. Adding "or confidence
< 0.5": 52 dear, 18 HARD misses.

CHOICE. The misses on FAILED are flat: the rule catches the same 3 ticks (19l,
9fc, k7p, all design at >= 0.84) at every T from 0.15 to 0.84. It misses the
same 7 (46x, dz1, nu9, us2, ef7, i1r, 823, all at dear mass <= 0.14). T
therefore sets only how many ticks start dear. 0.75 is the fewest dear starts
(22/96 = 23%, 20% of all 108) that still keeps every catch with margin for the
measured drift (0.84 - 0.09 = 0.75). It also matches wne's "above ~0.75 the
labels are ones a person would pick". Measured on HARD instead, 0.40 would be
the budget-bounded minimum (22 misses against 25 at 0.75). The difference is
3 long construction ticks, which is inside the classifier's noise.

HEADLINE FINDING: the mass does not predict hardness on this history.
AUC(mass -> HARD) = 0.42 and AUC(mass -> FAILED) = 0.45, where 0.5 means no
signal. Hard ticks carry less dear mass than easy ones (49-set 0.34 vs 0.41;
2jn 0.30 vs 0.42). The ticks that burned an hour (46x, dz1, 8v3, sg5, o0d,
sqx, z23, nu9) are big construction ticks at mass ~0. This rule will not
rescue them, and the escalate-after-failure ladder still will. Catching them
at the start needs a size/effort signal, not the work type.

CAVEATS. Only 10 real work failures. No tick has ever run on a cheap tier, so
"hard at strong" is not "would fail cheap". The re-asks read today's tick
text. The wall-clock kills in 9pd/dha/ncv came from a fixed 60-min clock.

CLOUD LADDER: NOT DECLARED here. The only Workers AI models proven through
pi in the container are glm-5.3 and glm-5.3-flash. A dear rung above glm-5.3
would need a model nobody has run in the image (candidates pi's catalog
carries: moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code, deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro-0813). The
alternative, flash start -> glm-5.3 dear, would move 80% of cloud ticks onto
flash. That is the operator's choice. The repo test's substrate list names
the cloud as the world still missing.
acceptance_criteria: Tier start uses Jev with role ticks skipped and a measured probability-mass threshold recorded in the tick; classifications replay on resume; with Jev unavailable the run starts at the policy default as today
closed_reason: Local ladder routes P(design)+P(diagnosis) > 0.75 (measured, see notes) to frontier; role ticks skipped, replay and fallback covered; cloud ladder follows in 7l1 pending the operator's model choice
